title: Export Disposition Matrix and SLA Mapping for High-Volume Enterprise Tenants
creator: Ravi Patel
description: Background: Enterprise customers repeatedly request tailored exports for usage analytics and cost breakdowns. Current intake lacks consistent disposition rules, causing long turnaround, unclear SLAs, and repeated engineering rework. Goal: Define a disposition matrix (routing + SLA) that classifies export requests by tenant size, data sensitivity, frequency, and compute cost, and wire it into the console intake flow and internal runbook so requests route automatically to self-serve, analytics ops, or scoped engineering projects.
goals: Create a disposition matrix that maps request attributes -> delivery lane (self-serve, ops-assisted, eng-project)
Define clear SLA bands for each lane (acknowledge, delivery ETA, escalation path)
Automate routing in the console intake form with pre-checks for PII/KMS and tenant capacity
Provide cost-estimate heuristics for exports and surface to customer during intake
Produce an internal runbook and allow export request telemetry to feed Console-Optimize recommendations
success_metrics: Reduce average time-to-first-delivery for enterprise exports from 21 days -> 5 days for ops-assisted lane
Increase % of exports handled via self-serve from 12% -> 40% for eligible tenants
Decrease engineering scoping tasks for ad-hoc exports by 60%
Track adoption: number of tenants using the new intake form and % completion of pre-approval checks
proposed_solution: Build a 4x4 disposition matrix (tenant scale x data sensitivity x requested frequency x compute complexity). Add intake fields in console for export type, approximate row count, frequency, intended recipients, and data classification. Implement an automated triage lambda that applies the matrix to return lane, SLA, cost estimate and required approvers. Low-sensitivity, low-cost exports route to immediate self-serve with templated BigQuery/CSV exports; medium sensitivity goes to Ops queue with 72h SLA; high sensitivity triggers Security/KMS review and scoped eng project with a standard intake packet.
tradeoffs: Tighter intake increases initial friction for customers but reduces long tail engineering work
Automated heuristics may misclassify edge cases => include override and appeal path
Building full pre-approval automation increases upfront engineering effort but should reduce ongoing ops cost
stakeholders: Eng: Miguel Alvarez (Analytics), Priya Sharma (Console Team)
acceptance_criteria: Disposition matrix documented in Confluence and approved by Security and Analytics leadership
Console intake form updated with new fields and front-end validation (Design sign-off)
Routing lambda prototypes triage requests consistently in a staging queue
SLA definitions published in runbook and visible in internal ticket creation templates
Cost-estimate heuristics implemented and surfaced to PM/CS preview dashboard
Telemetry events emitted for each intake attempt (successful classification, overrides, escalations)
